title: MediaTek 3Q26 revenue beats forecast, maintains peak-season momentum
content: MediaTek reported its September and third-quarter 2026 revenue results, with September revenue of NT$55.40 billion (approx. US$1.74 billion), down 13.69% from the previous month and up 1.97% from a year earlier. Third-quarter revenue reached NT$168.06 billion, up 10.43% quarter over quarter and 18.27% year over year, beating the upper end of its revenue forecast by about 5.2% and allowing the company to deliver the performance typically expected during the traditional peak season.

title: GlobalFoundries wins US$2 billion TSMC interposer deal, closing a US packaging gap

If confirmed, the result would strengthen Samsung's bid to supply memory for next-gen AI accelerators, though order timing and mass production plans remain unclear.

title: Applied Materials, Intel target AI chip bottlenecks with interconnect scaling and Foveros 3D
content: AI chip manufacturing demands are accelerating development of advanced logic and packaging technologies, prompting Applied Materials and Intel to expand their collaboration on next-generation transistors, interconnects, and advanced packaging.

title: Innodisk, Apacer post September 2026 revenue growth on AI demand
content: Memory module makers Innodisk and Apacer both reported year-over-year and month-over-month revenue growth for September 2026, supported by steady demand from industrial control, edge computing and AI smart connectivity applications. Their cumulative revenue for the first three quarters of the year also set strong growth records.

title: Ample revenue slips in September as passive component demand stays strong
content: Ample Electronic, a supplier of conductive paste materials for the passive components industry, reported September 2026 revenue of NT$304 million (approx. US$9.6 million), down 0.4% from August but up 76.3% from a year earlier. The company said strong demand for multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs) and related parts continued to support results, while third-quarter 2026 revenue rose to NT$879 million, up 23.6% quarter-over-quarter and 82% year-over-year.

title: Advantech tops US$1 billion in third-quarter revenue as edge AI orders climb
content: Advantech reported on October 7 that third-quarter consolidated revenue reached NT$32.44 billion (approx. US$1.02 billion), a record high as demand for edge AI, semiconductor equipment, and robotics stayed strong. September consolidated revenue rose to NT$10.749 billion, up 73.14% year-over-year, while cumulative revenue for the first nine months of 2026 increased to NT$78.952 billion from NT$52.961 billion a year earlier.

title: WinWay tops NT$10 billion in revenue as AI demand lifts third-quarter results
content: Semiconductor test interface maker WinWay Technology said AI and high-performance computing (HPC) demand, along with production-efficiency gains on some lines, drove shipments higher in 2026. The company surpassed NT$10 billion (approx. US$314.7 million) in cumulative revenue in September, a milestone it originally expected to hit in 2027, and reported record third-quarter sales as the semiconductor supply chain continued to benefit from strong AI-related spending.

title: Formosa Smart Energy teams up with CXIT on AI data center push
content: Formosa Smart Energy (FSET) is moving into AI data centers and will partner with Chuang-Xi Information and Technology (CXIT) to build one at Formosa Plastics Group's Mailiao industrial park, targeting Taiwanese enterprise users and Japanese cloud service providers (CSPs) in the first phase. The companies also plan to set up a CSP joint venture to run AI data center operations and computing-power services.

title: Interview: Europe's enterprise networking market returns to growth as pandemic inventory hangover clears
content: The European enterprise networking market has cleared its multi-year inventory digestion period. According to CONTEXT, sell-through via European distribution channels is growing in the low double digits entering 2026 across core infrastructure categories, including switches and enterprise wireless access points. That contrasts with the "heavy double-digit declines" the channel saw during COVID-19, said CONTEXT principal analyst Aaron Smith.
